summary: Jason views Uber as an 'anti-tariff stock' that is not impacted by trade disruptions and sees $88 as a key upside target.
quote: all that matters to me is that Uber is the anti-tariff stock. It just does great. It's not impacted by tariffs.

summary: Jason frames OpenAI's planned $2K–$20K/month AI agent pricing as evidence of a major new revenue opportunity as agentic computing becomes mainstream.
quote: OpenAI is planning to charge between $2K and $20K a month for different levels of AI agents. These would be basically cron jobs. They would run in the background and do things for your company that humans are doing right now.

summary: Aaron Levie (Box CEO) argues AI agents represent a massive TAM expansion for software companies like Box, as software shifts from seat-based pricing to capturing labor spend on work that was previously unaffordable or undone.
quote: now when your software actually brings the underlying workflow to the customer or the underlying outcome to the customer...all of a sudden you might be able to sell a multiple of the initial kind of 10 seats that you would've sold

summary: Sacks notes that Anthropic's Claude is the leader in coding assistance and is significantly powering the Manus agent demo, citing its strength in the most rapidly advancing AI application area.
quote: I think they're the leader, and in fact, I think the Manus demo that we showed...I think they are significantly using Anthropic for the code assistant part of it.

summary: Chamath says Claude is exceptional for code generation, which his firm uses as their primary model for that task.
quote: for most of our code gen, we use Anthropic and Claude kicks ass. It's exceptional.

summary: Chamath says his firm uses Gemini extensively and finds it incredible for many tasks, suggesting Google has a strong competitive AI product.
quote: We use Gemini, so for many tasks at 80.90, we use Gemini. It's incredible.
